appMemory.basis: PSS (Proportional Set Size) of the app process
appMemory.derivation: 5.75 GiB x 1024 = 5888 MiB (6174015488 bytes); soft = 0.8 x 5888 = 4710.4 MiB (PLAN A5: soft caps at 80%). The hard value is the platform kill limit and Meta says to target well below it; the soft value is where this project starts to act.

textureMemory.basis: GPU bytes of imported textures (ASTC 6x6 blocks, mip chain where enabled), as `node tools/assets/census.mjs --only texmem` counts them
textureMemory.justification: Textures share the PSS pool with everything else the process keeps (registry render-submission-economy), so their ceiling is a share of the app ceiling, stated with the headroom it leaves (registry shader-budget-authoring). These apps keep four resident classes: the engine and managed heap; render targets (two eye buffers and the passthrough composition); meshes and audio; textures. With no device reading of any of them, each class gets an equal quarter of the hard ceiling: textures consume at most 25%, and 75% is left for the other three. The share was set before any texture-memory reading was taken and is not fitted to one; H2 replaces the quarters with measured PSS.

display.binds: Quest 3 for fill: the same GPU shades more pixels per eye. No fill budget is stated here.

transparentLayersOverJar.reason: PLAN A5 sets no transparent-layer cap for Sundial; none is invented here

textureMaxSidePx.reason: soft: 80% of 1024 px is 819.2 px, which is no import size Unity offers, and PLAN A5 states none

caps.derivation: soft = 0.8 x hard (PLAN A5); the headsets do not enter these caps, they are the same on both

meta-memory-ram.title: Meta Horizon developer docs, Unity: Memory / RAM
meta-memory-ram.quote: Quest 3, Quest 3S: 5.75 GiB ... these limits are checked against your app's PSS, or Proportional Set Size

meta-quick-start.title: Meta Horizon developer docs: Quick start guide
meta-quick-start.quote: Proportional Set Size (PSS) kill limits are 4.4 GiB (Quest 2, Quest Pro) and 5.75 GiB (Meta VR Glasses, Quest 3, Quest 3S). Target well below these limits.

meta-refresh-rates.title: Meta Horizon developer docs, Unity: Set display refresh rates
meta-refresh-rates.quote: The default display refresh rate for apps is 72 Hz. Quest 3 and Quest 3S: 72, 80, 90, 100, 120 Hz; Quest 3 also above 120 Hz, up to 240 Hz, "not available on Meta Quest 3S". Frame budget 13.9 ms at 72 Hz, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz.

meta-compare-devices.title: Meta Horizon developer docs: Compare devices
meta-compare-devices.quote: Quest 3 and Quest 3S: 8 GB, Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2, 120 Hz; per eye 2064x2208 (Quest 3), 1832x1920 (Quest 3S)

plan-a5.quote: Budgets (hard caps; soft caps at 80%): Terrarium scene <= 40 draws, <= 60k tris, mean transparent layers over the jar <= 1.5; Sundial scene <= 30 draws, <= 30k tris; textures <= 1024 px; no post-processing

decision-0010.quote: A budget must hold on both, so where they differ, the lower one binds.

registry-render-submission-economy.subject: render-submission-economy
registry-render-submission-economy.quote: Residency is memory: every texture page, render target and font atlas the game keeps on the device, in a memory pool that the graphics processor shares with everything else the process holds.

registry-shader-budget-authoring.subject: shader-budget-authoring
registry-shader-budget-authoring.quote: state the budget for a class, state the share it is expected to consume, and state the headroom left over.
